AUTHOR: Fiorentino
TITLE: Deep Learning-Based Fish Detection in Challenging ROV Images: a YOLOv8 Approach for Offshore Environmental Monitoring
VENUE: 2026 34th Mediterranean Conference on Control and Automation (MED)
REGION: Offshore oil/gas platforms, Mediterranean Sea (Italy; ENI DECOPLAT project)
DATA: Own/partner ROV images from 9 offshore platforms (~2,600 images stated; Table I lists 1,629), expert bounding-box annotations
V_EV: Sec. III-A: 'Acquisitions span a wide range of operational depths (2-72 m), resulting in substantial variability in water color, visibility, and ambient illumination across subsets'
D2: 5-fold CV (80/20 per fold) within each of six composite platform datasets
D_EV: Sec. III-A: 'Each composite dataset was partitioned into five equal folds... fold Dk served as the test set while the union of the remaining four folds... constituted the training set'
R_EV: Table III: 'Average performance metrics across folds for the best model of each training configuration' (cross-validation within the same ROV dataset only)
C_EV: Sec. III-E: 'Model performance was assessed using standard object detection metrics, computed at a confidence threshold of 0.6 and an IoU threshold of 0.5.'
E_EV: Abstract: 'achieves a precision of 0.639, recall of 0.599, F1 score of 0.616, and mAP50 of 0.574' (detection metrics only)
ARCH: YOLOv8-Small and YOLOv8-Large with custom checkpoint-selection function
METR: Precision, recall, F1, mAP50, training time, CO2 footprint
NOTE: Folds are formed within composite platform datasets without stated grouping (images, likely frames from ROV video) -> k-fold(이미지); no leakage discussion (fold-5 lag attributed to distribution shift).
